founded.what: The year the house of Champagne Salon was founded, by its own site; its first vintage, the 1905, was made fifteen years before for the founder alone.

place: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Côte des Blancs, Champagne

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: beside its own plot it buys Chardonnay from about twenty parcels of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger and makes the wine itself.

story: Salon is the house of one wine. Its founder, Eugène-Aimé Salon (1867 to 1943), the son of a cartwright of the Marne by the house's account, made his name in the fur trade in Paris and wanted a Champagne of his own: Chardonnay alone, from the village of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger alone, from one harvest alone. His first vintage, the 1905, was made for himself, his family and his friends. In 1911, by one account, he bought a plot in the village, known since as the Jardin de Salon. The house dates itself from 1920 on its own site, the chronology of the Union des Maisons de Champagne giving 1914, and the 1921 is held to be the first vintage offered for sale. After his death in 1943 the house kept to his rule: one wine, made only in the years it declares, offered for sale about ten years after the harvest. From the 1970s it was fermented in stainless steel, with no malolactic conversion and no reserve wine, by Decanter's account. In 1988 or 1989, by differing accounts, it joined the Laurent-Perrier group, and its neighbour Delamotte became its sister house, taking its fruit in the years Salon is not made. The 2006 was its fortieth vintage, and the 2015 its forty fifth.

style.line: One wine and one style: Chardonnay of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger alone, from one harvest, fermented in steel and kept sharp, then released after about ten years, austere, high in acid and slow to open.
style.grapes: Chardonnay alone, from Le Mesnil-sur-Oger alone: the house's own plot, the Jardin de Salon, and about twenty other parcels in the village.
style.reserve: None: every bottle is of one harvest, and Decanter's account and the library both say the house uses no reserve wine.
style.vessels: Stainless steel since the 1970s, by Decanter's account; Vinous says the wine ferments entirely in steel.
style.malolactic: None: the malolactic conversion is blocked, by the accounts of Decanter and Vinous and the library.
style.lees: About ten years before release, by the house, which offers each vintage for sale some ten years after its harvest.
style.dosage: Low: 6 grams a litre for the 2012 by Decanter's preview, and 5 for the 1999 at its launch.

nv.note: Salon makes no non vintage wine at all: Le Mesnil is its only wine, and in the years it declares none, its fruit goes to Delamotte.

cuvee.name: Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs

first.what: The first vintage, made for the founder and his circle, by the house; the 1921 is held to be the first vintage offered for sale.

cuvee.rhythm: Made only in the years the house declares: by Decanter the 2006 was its fortieth vintage since 1905 and the 2012 its forty third; the 2013 was the forty fourth and the 2015 the forty fifth.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay alone, and never Pinot Noir or Meunier.
cuvee.sites: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger alone, a Grand Cru village of the Côte des Blancs: the house's own plot, the Jardin de Salon, and about twenty parcels across the village. It is a village wine, never a single vineyard.
cuvee.making: Each vintage is fermented in stainless steel, as it has been since the 1970s, with the malolactic conversion blocked and no reserve wine, by the accounts of Decanter and Vinous. The bottles then rest about ten years in the cellars before release, and the dosage is low, 6 grams a litre for the 2012.
cuvee.lees: About ten years before the wine is offered for sale, by the house.
cuvee.young: Lemon and lime zest over chalk, with spring blossom, a salty edge and a taut, mouth watering line that its years in the cellar have only begun to soften.
cuvee.aged: With long age it turns rich and deep: Decanter's vertical found black truffle and freshly ground coffee in the 1990, and the 1996 opening from lemon and sea salt in the glass.
cuvee.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, the Codex's range for sparkling wine, and never ice cold; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass.

table.house45: Salon is the house of one wine, at Le Mesnil-sur-Oger in the Côte des Blancs. Its founder, a Paris furrier born in the Marne, made his first vintage in 1905 for himself and his friends. The rule he set has held ever since. It is Chardonnay alone, from Le Mesnil alone, from one harvest alone. It is made only in the years the house declares, and the 2015 was only its forty fifth vintage. It is made in steel, kept sharp, and rests about ten years before release. There is no non vintage Salon, and its sister house next door is Delamotte.
table.house10: Salon is the one wine house of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, making vintage Chardonnay from one village in declared years alone.
table.cuvee45: Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs is the only wine Salon makes, a vintage Chardonnay from the Grand Cru village of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger. The house makes it only in the years it declares, about forty five times since 1905. It is fermented in steel and kept sharp, with no reserve wine, then rests about ten years before release. Expect lemon zest, chalk and spring blossom, with a salty edge and a taut line. With more years it grows deep, with notes of truffle and coffee. I serve it cool but never ice cold, in a tulip glass.
table.sale: If you want to taste one village in one year, Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs is the only wine Salon makes, and it waits about ten years before release. May I bring a bottle for the table?
table.cuvee10: Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs is Salon's only wine, vintage Chardonnay from the Grand Cru village of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger.
table.cuvee20: Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs is the one wine of Salon, Chardonnay from a single Grand Cru village, made only in declared years since 1905. It rests about ten years before release, and it arrives taut, chalky and long.

guests.q: Does Salon make a non vintage?
guests.a: No. Salon makes one wine, a vintage Blanc de Blancs from Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, and only in the years it declares; in other years its fruit goes to its sister house, Delamotte.

guests.q: Is Le Mesnil a single vineyard?
guests.a: No, it is a Grand Cru village of the Côte des Blancs. Salon draws on its own plot there and about twenty other parcels across the village.

guests.q: Why is it so rarely made?
guests.a: The house declares a vintage only when it judges the year worthy: the 2015 was only its forty fifth vintage since 1905.

traps: Salon makes no non-vintage wine at all: its only wine is the vintage Le Mesnil.
Le Mesnil-sur-Oger is a grand cru village, not a vineyard.
Salon and Delamotte share a village and an owner but are separate houses; in undeclared years Salon fruit can go to Delamotte.
Salon's Le Mesnil is a village wine, while Krug's Clos du Mesnil is a walled vineyard in the same village: two houses, two different wines.

sheet.label: Salon, S, Le Mesnil, Blanc de Blancs
sheet.note: They agree on the name. The label also prints Salon, the letter S, Blanc de Blancs and the vintage, and merchants list the wine as Cuvée S Le Mesnil or Salon Le Mesnil Blanc de Blancs.

questions.q: On the class sheet, which house's prestige cuvée is Le Mesnil?
questions.exp: Salon makes Le Mesnil and nothing else. Delamotte, its sister house, sits beside it on the sheet with a Blanc de Blancs, Krug's walled vineyard in the village is the Clos du Mesnil, and Taittinger's Blanc de Blancs is Comtes de Champagne.

questions.q: What becomes of Salon's Le Mesnil fruit in a year the house declares no vintage?
opts: It goes to its sister house, Delamotte
It is kept as reserve wine for a non vintage
It is sold under a second Salon label
It is left unpicked on the vine
questions.exp: In undeclared years Salon's fruit goes to Delamotte, its sister house next door. Salon keeps no reserve wine and makes no non vintage, so the fruit has no other Salon home.

questions.q: How is Salon's wine made, by the accounts of Decanter and Vinous?
opts: In stainless steel, with malolactic conversion blocked
In new oak barrels, with full malolactic conversion
In old casks, blended with reserve wines
In concrete eggs, after long skin contact
questions.exp: Salon ferments in stainless steel and blocks the malolactic conversion, which keeps the acid of Le Mesnil Chardonnay sharp, and it uses no reserve wine. Old oak and reserve wines are the marks of houses such as Bollinger and Krug.

report: founded.year departs from the library's 1921, which the library gives as the first commercial vintage rather than a founding: the record takes 1920 from the house's own site, gives the Union's 1914 beside it, and keeps 1921 as the first vintage held to have been sold.

The founder's dates, 1867 to 1943, rest on the group's own Salon papers (born 1867, a cartwright's son; his death in 1943) and agree with the search summaries of the history; a refuter should read a second independent source for them.
The fur trade rests on two secondary accounts read in one search; the 1911 purchase of the Jardin de Salon on one account, so the story says by one account.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the house buys fruit from parcels it does not own, so a refuter should read a back label.

The vintage counts (40th for 2006, 43rd for 2012, 44th for 2013, 45th for 2015) come from Decanter, Corney and Barrow and the house; they agree with each other, and the record gives no total for the twentieth century.
The group year is given as 1988 or 1989, since sources give both (and one 1987).
The cuvee name follows the plan's Le Mesnil with Blanc de Blancs, as merchants print it; the letter S on the label is the plan's note and a merchant's listing, not a label read.
No hectares are given for the Jardin de Salon, though one source says about one, since it is not a walled single vineyard of the kind the lint allows.
The library calls Salon the only house making a single wine from a single village in a single variety, a claim of an only; the record does not repeat it and calls Salon the house of one wine.
The library's line that the wine needs twenty years to soften is not repeated as a figure; the aged glass rests on Decanter's vertical.
